The alcohol is 75 ml before and after, and it has to end up as 25 per cent of the mixture. If the final mixture is M, then 75 = 0.25M, so M = 300 ml. The water added is 300 − 75 = 225 ml. The same result follows from the ratio: at 25 per cent alcohol the mixture is one part alcohol to three parts water, and three times 75 is 225.

question: If 35% of a number is 416 more than 27% of the same number, then the number is
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, 5200. Both percentages are taken of the same number, so they can be subtracted directly. 35 per cent less 27 per cent is 8 per cent, and that 8 per cent is the stated excess of 416. One per cent is therefore 416 ÷ 8 = 52, and the whole number is 52 × 100 = 5,200. Verifying: 35 per cent of 5,200 is 1,820, 27 per cent is 1,404, and 1,820 − 1,404 = 416.

question: In India, Cardamom Hills are regarded as a continuation of the
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, Western Ghats. The Cardamom Hills, called the Yela Mala locally, form the southern end of the Western Ghats, running across the Kerala-Tamil Nadu border south and east of the Anaimalai. Anaimudi, at about 2,695 metres the highest peak in peninsular India, stands at the knot where the Anaimalai, the Palani and the Cardamom hills meet, and the range continues southward to the Shencottah gap and the Agasthyamalai beyond it. The name comes from the spice the slopes have grown for centuries under the shade of the evergreen forest.

question: Match List–I with List–II and select the correct answer using the code given below the Lists: List–I (Tributary): A. Sutlej B. Kosi C. Teesta D. Chambal List–II (River): 1. Yamuna 2. Brahmaputra 3. Ganga 4. Indus Code:
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, A B C D : 4 3 2 1. The Sutlej is one of the five rivers of the Punjab and joins the Indus system, so A goes to 4. The Kosi drains eastern Nepal and north Bihar and empties into the Ganga near Kursela, so B goes to 3. The Teesta rises in north Sikkim and flows into the Brahmaputra in Bangladesh, so C goes to 2. The Chambal rises in the Vindhyan scarp near Mhow and joins the Yamuna in Etawah district, so D goes to 1. Only one option carries all four.

question: Which one of the following is the only riverine major port in India?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, Kolkata. Kolkata is the only riverine major port in India. It sits roughly 200 kilometres up the Hooghly from the Bay of Bengal, which is what gives it its reach into the eastern hinterland and also its permanent problem: the channel silts, so the approach has to be dredged continuously and the Farakka barrage was built in part to push more Ganga water down the Hooghly and keep it navigable. Because large modern vessels cannot come that far upstream, the port works as a twin system, with the Haldia Dock Complex nearer the sea handling the deeper-draught traffic.

question: Which one of the following is not a desert river?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, Barak. The Barak rises in the Manipur hills, flows west through Assam's Barak valley past Silchar, and crosses into Bangladesh, where it splits into the Surma and the Kushiyara and eventually feeds the Meghna. That is one of the wettest corners of India: the opposite of a desert regime in every respect. The other three are western Indian streams of the arid and semi-arid belt. The Rupen and the Machchhu drain into the Little Rann of Kachchh, and the Banas of north Gujarat ends in the Rann as well, all of them running dry for much of the year and dissipating inland instead of reaching the sea.

question: The heaviest rocks, which are rolled along the river bed in river transport, come under which type of load?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, Traction load. A river carries its load in four ways, and the division is by particle size and by how much energy the flow must spend on each. The heaviest fragments (cobbles and boulders) are never lifted clear of the bed at all; they are pushed, rolled and dragged along it, and that dragging is traction. Together with saltation it makes up what geologists call the bed load, as against the suspended and dissolved fractions that travel within the water itself.

question: Which of the following factors are needed for the growth of corals? 1. Freshwater 2. Clear shallow salt water 3. Plenty of sunlight for photosynthesis 4. Warm water between 23 °C and 25 °C Select the correct answer using the code given below.
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, 2, 3 and 4 only. Reef-building corals live with single-celled algae called zooxanthellae inside their tissues, and almost every growth requirement follows from that partnership. The algae photosynthesise, so the water must be shallow and clear enough for light to reach them: statements 2 and 3. The polyps build calcium carbonate skeletons fastest in warm water, which is statement 4. Fresh water is the one condition on the list that corals cannot tolerate: it dilutes the salinity they depend on and usually arrives loaded with silt that smothers the polyps. That is why reefs are absent at the mouths of large rivers and why statement 1 has to go, and only one option leaves it out.

question: Convection currents, which move the tectonic plates, are found in which layer of the earth?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, Mantle. Plate motion is driven by convection in the mantle. Heat from the decay of radioactive isotopes within the mantle, together with heat leaking out of the core, sets up slow cells in which hotter, less dense rock rises and cooler, denser rock sinks. The mantle is solid, but over geological time it deforms plastically, and the weak ductile layer just below the lithosphere (the asthenosphere) is where that flow is easiest. The plates ride on it and are dragged and pushed by it, helped by ridge push and by the pull of a cold slab sinking at a trench.

question: Consider the following statements: 1. The growth of socialist tendency in the national movement led to the foundation of the Congress Socialist Party in 1934 under the leadership of Acharya Narendra Deva and Jayaprakash Narayan. 2. In 1936, Jawaharlal Nehru urged the Congress to accept socialism as its goal and to bring itself closer to the peasantry and the working class. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, Both 1 and 2. The Congress Socialist Party was formed in 1934 by a younger group within the Congress (Acharya Narendra Deva as its president and Jayaprakash Narayan as general secretary, with Minoo Masani, Achyut Patwardhan, Asoka Mehta and Yusuf Meherally around them) after the Civil Disobedience Movement was suspended and many of them met in jail. That is statement 1. Statement 2 is equally well attested: at the Lucknow session of 1936, presiding over the Congress, Jawaharlal Nehru argued that the party should accept socialism as its goal and should build its links with the peasantry and the working class, and it was around that time that the Congress opened its doors formally to members of the peasant and labour organisations.

question: Initially, what was the purpose of setting up the hill stations during the colonial period in India?
opt_a: To serve as winter capitals for the British
opt_b: To serve the needs of the British army
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, To serve the needs of the British army. Hill stations were founded in the first instance as military posts. Simla grew out of the Anglo-Gurkha war of 1815-16, and the stations along the Himalayan foothills and in the Nilgiris were established to garrison troops in a climate the army believed suited European constitutions, at a safe altitude above the plains and near the frontiers that mattered. The other uses came later. They became sanatoria for sick and convalescent soldiers, then the seasonal seats of government (Simla was made the summer capital only in 1864) and finally resorts for planters, traders and officials on leave.

question: Who among the following founded the Dharma Sabha?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, Radhakanta Deb. The Dharma Sabha was set up in Calcutta in January 1830 by Radhakanta Deb, at the head of a group of orthodox Hindu gentry alarmed by the pace of reform. Its immediate business was to oppose Regulation XVII of 1829, by which Bentinck had made sati a punishable offence, and it carried an appeal against the ban all the way to the Privy Council in London, which rejected it in 1832. Its newspaper, the Samachar Chandrika, argued the conservative case against Rammohan Roy's Brahmo Sabha. Deb himself was not a simple obstructionist (he supported the spread of English education and the schooling of girls) but on questions touching custom and caste he stood with tradition.

question: Consider the following Jat peasant leaders of 17th and early 18th centuries: 1. Badan Singh 2. Raja Ram Jat 3. Gokula Jat 4. Churaman Jat Which one of the following is the correct chronological order of the above leaders?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, 3-2-4-1. The four leaders follow one another in an unbroken line of Jat resistance around Mathura and Agra. Gokula, a headman of Tilpat, led the rising of 1669 against Aurangzeb's revenue exactions and was executed at Agra the following year. Raja Ram took up the revolt from 1685 and was killed in 1688; the plundering of Akbar's tomb at Sikandra belongs to his years. Churaman, his nephew, built the resistance into something like a state, holding out from the fortress of Thun until his death in 1721. Badan Singh, who followed, consolidated that territory and founded the ruling house of Bharatpur, later raised to its height by his successor Suraj Mal. So the order runs Gokula, Raja Ram, Churaman, Badan Singh, which is 3-2-4-1.

question: Who among the following Bhakti saints did not belong to Nirguna School of Bhakti?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, Chaitanya. The Nirguna stream worships a divine without form or attributes, rejects images and temple ritual, and is generally indifferent to caste distinctions in worship; Kabir, Guru Nanak and Dadu Dayal all belong to it. Chaitanya does not. His devotion was to Krishna as a personal deity with a name, a form and a history, expressed through congregational singing, dance and the ecstatic kirtan processions of Nabadwip and Puri, and the Gaudiya Vaishnava tradition he founded made image worship central. Saguna bhakti is the label for that stream, and Chaitanya is one of its clearest examples.

question: Volcano Mount Merapi, which erupted in January 2021, is situated in
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, Indonesia. Mount Merapi stands on the boundary of Central Java and Yogyakarta, about 2,930 metres high and some 30 kilometres north of the city of Yogyakarta. It is among the most continuously active volcanoes anywhere, and it produced fresh lava avalanches and hot cloud emissions in January 2021, which is what puts it in this paper. Its position is not accidental: Indonesia sits where the Indo-Australian plate is being pushed under the Eurasian plate, a subduction zone along the Pacific Ring of Fire that has given the country more active volcanoes than any other.

question: E-100 pilot project, launched in Pune in June 2021, is related to the production and distribution of
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, ethanol. The E-100 pilot project was launched at Pune on 5 June 2021, World Environment Day, as a demonstration of a full chain for producing, storing and distributing ethanol as a motor fuel. It was announced alongside the report of the expert committee on the roadmap for ethanol blending, and alongside the decision to advance the target of 20 per cent ethanol in petrol from 2030 to 2025-26. The name is the giveaway once the convention is known: E followed by a number denotes the percentage of ethanol in the blend, so E-10 is a tenth ethanol and E-100 is the fuel in undiluted form.

question: On the occasion of the World Environment Day, 2021, which one of the following was declared as a National Park in India?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, Raimona. Raimona was declared a national park on 5 June 2021, World Environment Day, becoming the sixth in Assam. It covers the northern part of the Ripu Reserve Forest in Kokrajhar district, within the Bodoland Territorial Region, and its value lies in what it connects: Phipsoo Wildlife Sanctuary across the Bhutan border to the north and Buxa Tiger Reserve in West Bengal to the west, which together make one of the few surviving continuous forest corridors of the region. It is best known as golden langur habitat. The three other parks in the option set were all notified in the 1990s, well before the year in question.

question: Who among the following has withdrawn from the French Open Tennis Tournament, 2021 in second round after controversy over media obligations?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, Naomi Osaka. Before the 2021 French Open began, Osaka said she would not take part in post-match press conferences, arguing that the format could damage a player's mental health. She won her opening match, was fined by the tournament and warned of further sanction by the four Grand Slam bodies, and then withdrew rather than continue the dispute, disclosing at the same time that she had lived with depression since 2018. Her withdrawal came ahead of her second-round match, which is how the paper's phrasing should be read.

question: Heron drones, inducted by Indian forces for enhancing their surveillance capabilities, are acquired from
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, Israel. The Heron is a medium-altitude, long-endurance unmanned aircraft built by Israel Aerospace Industries, and India has flown it since the early 2000s alongside the smaller Searcher from the same maker. Its value to the Indian forces is endurance: it can stay airborne for a day or more, well above small-arms range, carrying electro-optical and radar sensors and relaying a live picture to a ground station. In the years around this paper the fleet was reinforced by the leased Heron TP variant for surveillance along the northern borders, and by an upgrade programme to extend the reach of the existing aircraft.

question: Cyclone 'Tauktae' was named by
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, Myanmar. Tauktae was the contribution of Myanmar to the list of cyclone names for the north Indian Ocean, the word referring to a highly vocal lizard. The storm formed in the Arabian Sea in May 2021 and crossed the Gujarat coast as an extremely severe cyclonic storm. Names in this basin are not invented at the time of the storm; they are taken in turn from a list assembled in advance, to which every member country of the regional panel contributes an equal number.

question: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below the Lists: List-I (Variant of COVID-19): A. Alpha, B. Beta, C. Gamma, D. Delta List-II (First identified in): 1. India, 2. Brazil, 3. Britain, 4. South Africa
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, A-3, B-4, C-2, D-1. The World Health Organization began labelling variants with Greek letters in May 2021, taking them in the order the variants were designated. Alpha was first identified in Britain, in Kent in late 2020, so A goes to 3. Beta was first reported from South Africa, which puts B at 4. Gamma came from Brazil, detected in travellers from the Amazonas region, so C is 2. Delta was first identified in India and drove the second wave there in the spring of 2021, so D is 1. Only one code carries all four.

question: Indian Coast Guard Offshore Patrol Vessel 'Sajag', which was commissioned in May 2021, was constructed by
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, M/s Goa Shipyard Limited. Sajag belongs to a series of offshore patrol vessels designed and built by Goa Shipyard Limited for the Indian Coast Guard, and it was commissioned in May 2021. Goa Shipyard is the defence public sector yard that specialises in exactly this class: patrol vessels of a few thousand tonnes with a helicopter deck, built for long endurance rather than for heavy weapons, and used for exclusive economic zone surveillance, anti-smuggling work, pollution response and search and rescue. The names in the series follow a pattern of their own, Shaunak, Sujeet, Sarthak, Sajag and Sujay among them.

question: Who among the following was the Head of the Expert Committee on Variable Capital Company in India which has submitted its report recently?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, K. P. Krishnan. The International Financial Services Centres Authority set up an expert committee to examine whether the Variable Capital Company could be brought into Indian law for the international financial services centre at GIFT City, and the committee was headed by K. P. Krishnan, a former civil servant long associated with financial sector reform. Its report recommended enabling the structure so that funds set up in the centre could operate with the flexibility their competitors abroad already had.

question: Which one of the following States ranked first on Sustainable Development Goal India Index, 2020-21 released by NITI Aayog?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, Kerala. Kerala took first place among the States in the SDG India Index 2020-21, the third edition, released by NITI Aayog in June 2021. It had also topped the two earlier editions, and its lead comes from the goals on health, education, water and sanitation, where its long record on social indicators shows up directly in the scoring. Himachal Pradesh and Tamil Nadu came next, closely behind, and Bihar was at the bottom of the State list.

question: Which one of the following is the theme of the World Ocean Day, 2021?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, The Ocean : Life and Livelihoods. That was the United Nations theme for World Oceans Day on 8 June 2021, chosen to mark the start of the UN Decade of Ocean Science for Sustainable Development, which runs from 2021 to 2030. The wording points at the two things the observance is meant to hold together: the ocean as a living system and the hundreds of millions of people whose work depends on it. What makes this item unusually fair is that the other three options are not invented; each was the theme of another year.

question: In the latest Chandler Good Government Index (CGGI), which classifies 104 countries in terms of government capabilities and outcomes, India has been ranked
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, 49th. India stood 49th among the 104 countries covered by the Chandler Good Government Index, published by the Chandler Institute of Governance in Singapore. The index is unusual in what it measures, not the quality of democracy or the level of corruption alone, but the capability of a government to do its job, scored across seven pillars covering leadership and foresight, laws and policies, institutions, financial stewardship, the marketplace it creates, its global influence and reputation, and whether it helps people rise. Finland headed the first edition, with the Nordic countries and Singapore near the top.

question: Scientists at CSIR-NCL Pune, with support from the Water Technology Initiative of the Department of Science and Technology (DST), Government of India, have recently developed a novel hybrid technology to bring safe and healthy drinking water. What is the name of the hybrid technology?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, SWASTIIK. SWASTIIK is the hybrid water-disinfection technology developed at the National Chemical Laboratory in Pune under the Department of Science and Technology's water technology initiative. What makes it hybrid is the pairing of two effects: hydrodynamic cavitation, in which collapsing bubbles in a flowing stream generate the shock and heat that kill microorganisms, together with natural additives from plant oils that improve the kill rate at lower energy. The aim was a chemical-free method that could be run at community scale without leaving disinfection by-products in the water.
